questions.prompt: Define skew as capture-clock arrival minus launch-clock arrival. With all other delays fixed, adding +10 ps skew changes setup and same-edge hold slack how?
questions.answer: A later capture edge gives the max-delay path more time before the next capture deadline, adding to setup slack. The same late capture clock also keeps the receiver vulnerable longer to the new fastest data launched on that cycle, subtracting from hold slack. Under this convention every additional picosecond of skew adds one picosecond to setup slack and removes one from hold slack, before other analysis changes. Check both equations rather than calling all skew either good or bad.
questions.hint: Place both the next capture edge and the same-cycle capture edge on the timing axis.
questions.followup: Which assumption would you verify first in simulation, and why?
questions.trap: A correct equation is useful only within its stated operating conditions.
choices: Setup +10 ps; hold −10 ps
Both −10 ps
Setup −10 ps; hold +10 ps
Both +10 ps
choiceExplanations: A later capture edge extends the setup deadline but also extends the same-edge hold protection window.
Setup receives more available time under the stated convention.
This uses the opposite skew sign convention.
The same late clock cannot simultaneously lend time to setup and shorten hold vulnerability.
questions.mcqExplanation: A later capture edge extends the setup deadline but also extends the same-edge hold protection window.
questions.oralPrompt: With skew defined as capture-clock arrival minus launch-clock arrival, explain why increasing positive skew helps setup but hurts same-edge hold.

questions.title: Driver plus distributed-wire Elmore moment
questions.prompt: Use τE = Rd(Cw+CL) + Rw(Cw/2+CL). Given Rd=1 kΩ, Rw=200 Ω, Cw=80 fF and CL=20 fF, what is τE?
questions.answer: The driver term is 1000×100 fF = 100 ps. The distributed-wire term is 200×(40+20) fF = 12 ps. The total is **112 ps**. This is the stated Elmore moment, not automatically a measured 50% propagation delay.
questions.hint: Keep the driver’s total capacitive load separate from the distributed wire’s weighted load.
questions.followup: Which assumption would you verify first in simulation, and why?
questions.trap: A correct equation is useful only within its stated operating conditions.
choices: 120 ps
112 ps
60 ps
choiceExplanations: This assigns full Cw rather than Cw/2 to the wire-resistance term.
The driver term is 100 ps and the wire term is 12 ps.
This multiplies 112 ps by 0.69, which the requested Elmore expression does not specify.
This incorrectly halves the capacitance seen by the driver as well.
questions.mcqExplanation: τE=1000×100 fF + 200×60 fF = 112 ps. This is the stated Elmore moment, not automatically the measured 50% delay.
questions.oralPrompt: Use τE = Rd(Cw+CL) + Rw(Cw/2+CL). Given Rd = 1 kΩ, Rw = 200 Ω, Cw = 80 fF and CL = 20 fF, calculate τE in ps.

questions.title: Investigate a routed timing regression
questions.prompt: Cells and placement are unchanged, but a critical path becomes slower after detailed routing. What should be inspected before deciding to upsize?
questions.answer: Compare estimated and extracted net resistance/capacitance, actual detours, routing layers, via counts, coupling environment and endpoint load. Check whether input slew changed and how the library delay calculation responded. Inspect congestion and pin-access restrictions near the bad nets. Resizing may be useful for a driver-limited path, but it cannot be assumed to fix a long detour or an inaccessible pin, and its added input capacitance can worsen the preceding stage.
questions.hint: Unchanged placement does not imply unchanged electrical interconnect.
questions.followup: Which assumption would you verify first in simulation, and why?
questions.trap: A correct equation is useful only within its stated operating conditions.
choices: Only endpoint load, treating distributed resistance and aggressor switching as negligible by default.
Only total wire length, since different layers and via counts cannot change resistance at fixed length.
Extracted net R/C, detours, layers, vias, coupling and resulting input slew along the path.
Only cell arc tables, because unchanged cells imply the same input slew after routing.
choiceExplanations: Distributed RC and coupling may be exactly what created the regression.
Layers, cross sections and vias affect resistance and capacitance.
Routing changes parasitic loads and transitions even with identical cells and placement.
Routed loading can change input slews and therefore cell delays.
questions.mcqExplanation: Find whether the new delay is wire-, driver- or slew-limited. Upsizing may help one segment while loading its predecessor more heavily.
questions.oralPrompt: A critical path regresses after detailed routing even though its cells and placement are unchanged. What evidence would you inspect before resizing?

questions.title: Parallel scan-chain loading time
questions.prompt: There are 1200 scan registers in four equal parallel chains, shifted at 20 MHz. Ignoring capture and unload, how long to load one scan state?
questions.answer: Each chain contains 300 registers. All four chains shift in parallel, so loading requires 300 cycles, not 1200. At 20 MHz each cycle is 50 ns; total time is **15 µs**. If chains are unbalanced, the longest chain determines the shift length.
questions.hint: Use the longest chain length, since all four chains shift together.
questions.followup: Which assumption would you verify first in simulation, and why?
questions.trap: A correct equation is useful only within its stated operating conditions.
choices: 60 µs
30 µs
15 µs
choiceExplanations: 60 µs treats all 1200 bits as one serial chain.
30 µs adds an unload despite the stated load-only calculation.
Each chain is 300 bits and one cycle is 50 ns, so 300×50 ns=15 µs.
Dividing by four again double-counts the parallel-chain benefit.
questions.mcqExplanation: Each chain is 300 bits and one cycle is 50 ns, so 300×50 ns=15 µs.
questions.oralPrompt: There are 1200 scan registers in four equal parallel chains. Shift clock is 20 MHz. How many µs are required to load one complete scan state? Ignore capture and unload.

questions.title: What does 99% stuck-at coverage establish?
questions.prompt: An ATPG report states 99% stuck-at fault coverage. Which conclusion is defensible?
questions.answer: **Choose B.** The report describes coverage of its specified stuck-at model under its assumptions and exclusions. It does not prove functional correctness, at-speed operation or coverage of every physical defect. Inspect the definition of the denominator and treatment of untestable or excluded faults before comparing percentages across flows.
questions.hint: Start by stating the model, the operating condition and the quantity being measured.
questions.followup: Which assumption would you verify first in simulation, and why?
questions.trap: A correct equation is useful only within its stated operating conditions.
choices: The design is functionally correct for 99% of all programs
Most faults in the reported stuck-at model were detected under the test assumptions
The design is guaranteed to meet functional clock frequency
All remaining silicon failures must be packaging defects

labs.title: Parse engineering units
labs.lesson: EDA reports mix ps, ns, fF and scientific notation. Normalize to SI before comparing numbers. Python `re.fullmatch` validates the entire field; `math.isfinite` rejects NaN and infinity. Raise `ValueError` for malformed or unknown units. A failed measurement must never become zero.
labs.prompt: Implement `parse_value(text)`. Accept a signed finite number and one of s, ns, ps, F, fF, A, uA, nA, V. Return the value in SI units. Reject invalid text and unsupported units.
hints: Use a dictionary mapping unit strings to scale factors.
Validate the whole input, not just a number substring.
Normalize first, then check finiteness.
labs.explain: The unit lookup makes the conversion explicit. A strict full match catches trailing garbage. This prevents stale, failed or mislabeled results from silently entering a timing table.

labs.title: Calculate setup & hold slack
labs.lesson: Use capture-minus-launch skew. Setup slack is T + skew − (tcq_max + data_max + setup + uncertainty_setup). Hold slack is tcq_min + data_min − (skew + hold + uncertainty_hold). All inputs in this exercise are ps. Positive skew helps setup and hurts hold.
labs.prompt: Return `(setup_slack, hold_slack)` from `slacks(T, skew, cq_max, d_max, setup, u_setup, cq_min, d_min, hold, u_hold)`. Do not put T into the hold equation.
labs.starter:
def slacks(T, skew, cq_max, d_max, setup, u_setup, cq_min, d_min, hold, u_hold):
    raise NotImplementedError
hints: Draw launch at zero and capture at skew.
Compare arrival time with required time.
Increasing only T must leave hold slack unchanged.
labs.explain: The second test is a physical check: slowing the clock improves setup while the same-edge hold race remains.

labs.title: Estimate a driver and its load
labs.lesson: For the first-order RC model, t50 = ln(2) R (Cint + Cload). Scaling width by s makes R/s and Cint·s. This teaching model ignores input slew, short-channel effects and wiring. Return seconds; parameters use SI.
labs.prompt: Implement `delay(r, cint, cload, scale=1)` and reject nonpositive resistance/scale or negative capacitances.
labs.starter:
def delay(r, cint, cload, scale=1):
    raise NotImplementedError
labs.tests:
import math
assert math.isclose(delay(2000,3e-15,12e-15),math.log(2)*30e-12)
assert math.isclose(delay(2000,3e-15,12e-15,2),math.log(2)*18e-12)
try: delay(2000,3e-15,12e-15,0)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError("Zero width is invalid")
print("PASS: load, intrinsic capacitance and width scaling")
hints: The scaled driver also has more intrinsic capacitance.
Convert kΩ and fF before multiplication.
labs.explain: Width scaling improves only the external-load term in this idealized expression. The intrinsic RC product stays constant; upstream loading is an additional cost omitted here.

labs.title: Find the correct waveform crossing
labs.lesson: Sampled waveforms require interpolation. Search adjacent sample pairs that bracket the target in the requested direction. Rising uses v0 < threshold ≤ v1; falling uses v0 > threshold ≥ v1. Linear interpolation estimates time inside that interval. Missing crossings are measurement failures.
labs.prompt: Implement `crossing(times, volts, threshold, edge="rise", occurrence=1)`. Return crossing time in seconds. Reject unequal/short arrays, nonincreasing time, unknown edge, and invalid occurrence. Raise ValueError when no requested crossing exists.
labs.starter:
def crossing(times, volts, threshold, edge="rise", occurrence=1):
    raise NotImplementedError
hints: Count only direction-qualified brackets.
Interpolation fraction is (threshold − v0)/(v1 − v0).
Do not return zero when a crossing is missing.
labs.explain: Explicit occurrence protects against measuring precharge or an earlier cycle. In a real testbench, also restrict the time window and inspect slew/compression sensitivity.

labs.title: Check both ROM keeper margins
labs.lesson: A keeper restores a retained high bit but opposes selected discharge. In a constant-current teaching model: high droop = max(Ileak − Ik, 0)t/C; low swing = max(Ion − Ik − Iopp, 0)t/C. Keep-high passes if droop ≤ budget; discharge passes if swing ≥ target. Currents in A, time in s, capacitance in F.
labs.prompt: Implement `rom_pass(c, time, leak, keeper, on, opposing, max_droop, min_swing)` returning two booleans `(high_pass, low_pass)`.
labs.starter:
def rom_pass(c, time, leak, keeper, on, opposing, max_droop, min_swing):
    raise NotImplementedError
labs.tests:
assert rom_pass(100e-15,1e-9,2e-6,5e-6,25e-6,0,.05,.15)==(True,True)
assert rom_pass(100e-15,1e-9,2e-6,20e-6,25e-6,0,.05,.15)==(True,False)
assert rom_pass(50e-15,1e-9,4e-6,1e-6,25e-6,0,.05,.15)==(False,True)
print("PASS: keeper protects high and competes with low")
hints: Clamp net current to zero for this simplified model.
Test a keeper that is too strong and one that is too weak.
labs.explain: This detects opposite failure directions. Real margin checks use voltage-dependent currents, extracted bitlines, patterns, sense timing, PVT and local mismatch.

labs.title: Interpolate a Liberty table
labs.lesson: NLDM delay depends on input slew and output load. Bilinear interpolation blends the four surrounding samples. This exercise requires sorted two-point axes; extrapolation is rejected rather than silently inventing a value.
labs.prompt: Implement `interpolate(xs, ys, values, x, y)`, where values[i][j] belongs to xs[i],ys[j]. Each axis has two strictly increasing points; return the bilinear value for an in-range query.
labs.starter:
def interpolate(xs, ys, values, x, y):
    raise NotImplementedError
hints: x fraction is 0.25; y fraction is 0.75 for the main case.
Interpolate load first at each slew, then interpolate those results in slew.
labs.explain: At 10 ps slew the interpolated delay is 35 ps; at 30 ps it is 48 ps. Blending by 0.25 gives 38.25 ps. Axis orientation is part of model correctness.

labs.title: Build a reproducible sweep manifest
labs.lesson: A regression is trustworthy only if you know which cases should exist. Cartesian products enumerate cell×corner×slew×load. Use immutable tuple keys; duplicates in inputs must not produce duplicate jobs. Deterministic ordering makes diffs useful.
labs.prompt: Implement `manifest(cells, corners, slews, loads)` returning a sorted list of unique `(cell, corner, slew, load)` tuples.
labs.starter:
def manifest(cells, corners, slews, loads):
    raise NotImplementedError
labs.tests:
m=manifest(["INV","NAND","INV"],["ss","ff"],[10,20],[2,6])
assert len(m)==16 and len(set(m))==16
assert m==sorted(m)
assert manifest([], ["ss"], [10],[2])==[]
assert ("NAND","ss",20,6) in m
print("PASS: coverage, duplicates, determinism and empty inputs")
hints: Use itertools.product for combinations.
A set removes duplicate tuples; sorted restores deterministic order.
labs.explain: In production, add state/arc/seed/revision to the key and fail explicitly on unexpectedly empty collections. A deterministic manifest is the contract against which outputs are checked.

labs.title: Audit missing, duplicate and invalid results
labs.lesson: Exit code zero does not prove that every measurement is valid. Compare results against the expected manifest; detect missing, unexpected and duplicate keys, and reject non-finite values. The following API assumes records are dictionaries with `key` and `value`.
labs.prompt: Implement `audit(expected, records)` returning a dictionary with sorted lists `missing`, `extra`, `duplicate`, `invalid`. A repeated key is duplicate even if values agree. Invalid includes nonnumeric and nonfinite values.
hints: Counter finds duplicate keys.
Set differences find missing and unexpected outputs.
Do not coerce failed text to zero.
labs.explain: Report categories independently: a duplicate can also be invalid. Real release checks additionally require timestamps, tool/model revisions, units and convergence evidence.

labs.title: Calculate an array failure budget
labs.lesson: Under independent identical bit failures, array yield Y=(1−p)^N. Solve p = 1−Y^(1/N). For large N, direct subtraction loses precision. Use `-expm1(log(Y)/N)`. This is a model; spatial correlation, repairs and systematic failures change the relationship.
labs.prompt: Implement `bit_budget(bits, yield_target)` for positive integer bits and 0 < yield_target ≤ 1. Return maximum per-bit failure probability.
labs.tests: import math p=bit_budget(1_000_000,.99) assert math.isclose(p,1.00503358e-8,rel_tol=1e-7) assert math.isclose(bit_budget(1,.9),.1) assert bit_budget(1000,1)==0 assert bit_budget(2_000_000,.99)
hints: Take natural logarithms to isolate p.
Use expm1 when subtracting a number very close to one.
labs.explain: Larger arrays demand rarer per-bit failures. This is why a few nominal simulations cannot demonstrate a high-sigma memory yield target.

labs.title: Implement a modular NTT butterfly
labs.lesson: An NTT butterfly computes t=(b·w) mod q, then outputs ((a+t) mod q,(a−t) mod q). Python `%` with positive q returns a nonnegative residue. The hardware implementation must define signedness, widths, reduction and latency; a Python reference is the comparison oracle.
labs.prompt: Implement `butterfly(a,b,w,q)` with q > 1. Normalize results to [0,q).
labs.starter:
def butterfly(a, b, w, q):
    raise NotImplementedError
labs.tests:
assert butterfly(5,3,4,17)==(0,10)
assert butterfly(0,0,3,17)==(0,0)
assert butterfly(1,16,16,17)==(2,0)
for a in range(17):
    x,y=butterfly(a,3,4,17)
    assert 0<=x<17 and 0<=y<17 and (x+y)%17==(2*a)%17
print("PASS: negative difference, modular product and butterfly invariant")
hints: Reduce b*w before adding/subtracting.
Check the sum invariant (x+y) mod q = 2a mod q.
labs.explain: The small q=17 example is illustrative, not the project modulus. Use the actual report configuration and verified throughput scope when defending the hardware.

labs.title: Rank validated timing regressions
labs.lesson: A useful regression comparison matches case identity and normalizes units before ranking. This exercise works on pre-normalized ps values, rejects bad measurements, and reports current−baseline so positive values mean a slowdown.
labs.prompt: Implement `regressions(baseline, current)` for dictionaries mapping case names to ps delays. Return common cases as `(name, delta)` sorted by descending delta, then name. Reject nonfinite or negative delay in either dictionary.
hints: Compare only the intersection of case keys.
Sort with key (-delta, name).
labs.explain: Missing and extra cases need the separate audit from Lab 8; ranking the intersection does not prove coverage. Conditions and model revisions must match before interpreting deltas.

labs.title: Estimate precharge recovery time
labs.lesson: An RC precharge from V0 toward VDD follows V(t)=VDD−(VDD−V0)e^(−t/RC). Solving for time to reach target: t=−RC ln((VDD−target)/(VDD−V0)). Reaching exactly VDD takes infinite time in this ideal model.
labs.prompt: Implement `precharge_time(r,c,vdd,v0,target)`, requiring r,c > 0 and 0 ≤ v0 ≤ target < vdd. Return seconds.
labs.tests:
import math
assert math.isclose(precharge_time(2000,100e-15,1,0,.9),2e-10*math.log(10))
assert precharge_time(2000,100e-15,1,.5,.5)==0
try: precharge_time(2000,100e-15,1,0,1)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError("Exact rail cannot be reached in finite time")
print("PASS: 90% recovery, initial voltage and impossible target")
hints: Rearrange the exponential before taking ln.
The target must stay strictly below VDD.
labs.explain: Back-to-back ROM reads must include this recovery interval. Passing one isolated access after long idle is insufficient evidence of cycle-time feasibility.

eecs427:l02_p02_b.name: l02_p02_b
eecs427:l02_p02_b.caption: The MOS gate stack is a capacitor, and the gate voltage relative to the body controls whether a channel forms between n+ source and drain.
eecs427:l02_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p03_t.name: l02_p03_t
eecs427:l02_p03_t.caption: Static CMOS pairs a pMOS pull-up network with a complementary nMOS pull-down network, so exactly one of them conducts in steady state.
eecs427:l02_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p03_b.name: l02_p03_b
eecs427:l02_p03_b.caption: In a NAND2 the internal node Z between the two series nMOS takes different values depending on the input pattern, including a degraded VDD−Vth.
eecs427:l02_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p04_t.name: l02_p04_t
eecs427:l02_p04_t.caption: In a NOR2 the internal node between the series pMOS can sit at a degraded Vth or float near VDD.
eecs427:l02_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p04_b.name: l02_p04_b
eecs427:l02_p04_b.caption: A tristate buffer drives 0 or 1 when enabled and presents high impedance Z when not enabled.
eecs427:l02_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p05_b.name: l02_p05_b
eecs427:l02_p05_b.caption: A tristate inverter puts EN-controlled transistors in series with an inverter stack, so its output is restored to the rails.
eecs427:l02_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p06_b.name: l02_p06_b
eecs427:l02_p06_b.caption: On a p-substrate the nMOS sits directly in the substrate while the pMOS needs an n-well as its body.
eecs427:l02_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p07_t.name: l02_p07_t
eecs427:l02_p07_t.caption: Metal on lightly doped silicon makes a poor contact, so heavily doped n+ well taps and p+ substrate taps tie the bodies to VDD and GND.
eecs427:l02_p07_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p07_b.name: l02_p07_b
eecs427:l02_p07_b.caption: The inverter is defined by a set of masks, and the cross-section is taken along the dashed line through both transistors and both taps.
eecs427:l02_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p08_t.name: l02_p08_t
eecs427:l02_p08_t.caption: Six masks define the inverter: n-well, polysilicon, n+ diffusion, p+ diffusion, contact and metal.
eecs427:l02_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p11_t.name: l02_p11_t
eecs427:l02_p11_t.caption: Photolithography transfers the mask pattern into photoresist, and the resist then protects the oxide during etch.
eecs427:l02_p11_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p15_t.name: l02_p15_t
eecs427:l02_p15_t.caption: N-diffusion is self-aligned: the already-patterned poly gate blocks the implant, so source and drain line up exactly with the gate.
eecs427:l02_p15_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p17_b.name: l02_p17_b
eecs427:l02_p17_b.caption: Contacts connect M1 to diffusion and poly, and vias connect each metal layer up through the stack to top metal.
eecs427:l02_p17_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p18_t.name: l02_p18_t
eecs427:l02_p18_t.caption: Minimum mask dimensions set transistor size, and the feature size is the minimum poly width, which sets L_gate.
eecs427:l02_p18_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p18_b.name: l02_p18_b
eecs427:l02_p18_b.caption: Design rules exist to tolerate fabrication errors such as mask misalignment, dust, lateral diffusion and rough surfaces.
eecs427:l02_p18_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p19_t.name: l02_p19_t
eecs427:l02_p19_t.caption: A transistor is the overlap of poly and diffusion, so poly must extend past diffusion, and diffusion should never be used for routing.
eecs427:l02_p19_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p19_b.name: l02_p19_b
eecs427:l02_p19_b.caption: The inverter layout annotates the key rule types: poly extension, contact to diffusion, n-well enclosure of p-diffusion, metal spacing and poly-to-contact spacing.
eecs427:l02_p19_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p20_t.name: l02_p20_t
eecs427:l02_p20_t.caption: Contact and via rules require both layers to enclose the cut so that a misaligned mask still lands the contact on both materials.
eecs427:l02_p20_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p20_b.name: l02_p20_b
eecs427:l02_p20_b.caption: Plasma processing charges exposed conductors, and if a large conductor area connects only to a thin gate the gate oxide can break down.
eecs427:l02_p20_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p21_t.name: l02_p21_t
eecs427:l02_p21_t.caption: Antenna violations are fixed by jumping to a higher metal near the gate or by adding a reverse-biased diode to discharge the line.
eecs427:l02_p21_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p21_b.name: l02_p21_b
eecs427:l02_p21_b.caption: The parasitic vertical PNP and lateral NPN form a thyristor that, once triggered through Rwell and Rsub, latches a low-impedance VDD-to-GND path.
eecs427:l02_p21_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p22_t.name: l02_p22_t
eecs427:l02_p22_t.caption: Latch-up is avoided by lowering well and substrate resistance with heavy doping, close taps and guard rings.
eecs427:l02_p22_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p22_b.name: l02_p22_b
eecs427:l02_p22_b.caption: In 130 nm the minimum device is 160 nm wide by 120 nm long, the reference inverter is 320/120 pMOS over 160/120 nMOS, and NAND2/NOR2 share diffusion between adjacent transistors.
eecs427:l02_p22_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p23_t.name: l02_p23_t
eecs427:l02_p23_t.caption: A simplified layout diagram shows only metal1, p-diffusion, n-diffusion, poly and contacts for the inverter and a three-input gate.
eecs427:l02_p23_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p23_b.name: l02_p23_b
eecs427:l02_p23_b.caption: A stick diagram has no dimensions and shows only the relative positions of transistors, wires and contacts.
eecs427:l02_p23_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l02_p25_t.name: l02_p25_t
eecs427:l02_p25_t.caption: Yield is good dies divided by total dies, dies per wafer falls with die area including an edge-loss term, and yield falls exponentially with area times defect density.
eecs427:l02_p25_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p02_b.name: l03_p02_b
eecs427:l03_p02_b.caption: Propagation delay is measured from the 50% point of the input to the 50% point of the output, and rise and fall times from 10% to 90%.
eecs427:l03_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p03_t.name: l03_p03_t
eecs427:l03_p03_t.caption: A step into an RC network gives an exponential output that crosses 50% at t = ln2·RC ≈ 0.69RC.
eecs427:l03_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p03_b.name: l03_p03_b
eecs427:l03_p03_b.caption: For a low-to-high output the pMOS charges CL through RP, and for high-to-low the nMOS discharges CL through RN.
eecs427:l03_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p04_t.name: l03_p04_t
eecs427:l03_p04_t.caption: The equivalent resistance averages V/I at the start and midpoint of the transition and is about three quarters of VDD over IDSAT.
eecs427:l03_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p05_t.name: l03_p05_t
eecs427:l03_p05_t.caption: Gate capacitance is modeled simply as Cox·W·L, which is about 1.3 fF per micron of gate width in this process.
eecs427:l03_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p05_b.name: l03_p05_b
eecs427:l03_p05_b.caption: Source and drain diffusion capacitance is parasitic, depends on area and perimeter, and is about CG for a contacted diffusion and half that for an uncontacted one.
eecs427:l03_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p06_t.name: l03_p06_t
eecs427:l03_p06_t.caption: Good layout shares contacted diffusions and merges uncontacted ones, which in the NAND3 example cuts output capacitance by 2C.
eecs427:l03_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p06_b.name: l03_p06_b
eecs427:l03_p06_b.caption: In 130 nm, C is about 1.3 fF per micron so 0.21 fF per unit device, and R is about 13 kΩ for a 160 nm wide unit nMOS.
eecs427:l03_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p07_t.name: l03_p07_t
eecs427:l03_p07_t.caption: A fanout-of-1 inverter with 10 kΩ drive and 1.26 fF total load has a delay of about 8.7 ps.
eecs427:l03_p07_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p08_t.name: l03_p08_t
eecs427:l03_p08_t.caption: Delay falls with VDD roughly as CL·VDD over (VDD−VT) to the alpha, with alpha about 1.2 to 1.3.
eecs427:l03_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p08_b.name: l03_p08_b
eecs427:l03_p08_b.caption: For a fixed load, upsizing the driver by S reduces delay toward an asymptote set by its own intrinsic capacitance.
eecs427:l03_p08_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p09_t.name: l03_p09_t
eecs427:l03_p09_t.caption: Raising the P/N ratio beta speeds up the rising transition but slows the falling one, so average tp has a minimum, which is not at the tr = tf point.
eecs427:l03_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p09_b.name: l03_p09_b
eecs427:l03_p09_b.caption: NAND2 rising delay is 0.69 Rp/2 CL if both inputs fall but 0.69 Rp CL if only one falls, and falling delay is 0.69 2Rn CL.
eecs427:l03_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p10_t.name: l03_p10_t
eecs427:l03_p10_t.caption: Placing the late-arriving input on the transistor closest to the output means the internal node is already discharged when it switches.
eecs427:l03_p10_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p10_b.name: l03_p10_b
eecs427:l03_p10_b.caption: Size each network so its worst-case path has the resistance of the reference inverter: NAND2 nMOS 2 and pMOS 2, NOR2 pMOS 4 and nMOS 1.
eecs427:l03_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p11_t.name: l03_p11_t
eecs427:l03_p11_t.caption: For OUT = NOT(D + A(B+C)) the series paths set the widths, and there are multiple valid pMOS sizings such as 4-8-8-4 or 3-6-6-6.
eecs427:l03_p11_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p11_b.name: l03_p11_b
eecs427:l03_p11_b.caption: Elmore delay sums, for each node, its capacitance times the total resistance from that node back to the source.
eecs427:l03_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p12_t.name: l03_p12_t
eecs427:l03_p12_t.caption: A unit NAND3 driving f identical gates has worst-case falling delay (10.5 + 5f)RC and pull-up delay (9 + 5f)RC by Elmore.
eecs427:l03_p12_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p12_b.name: l03_p12_b
eecs427:l03_p12_b.caption: Two NAND2 stick layouts differ in whether the output sits on a shared middle pMOS diffusion or on two outer diffusions, which changes output capacitance.
eecs427:l03_p12_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l03_p13_t.name: l03_p13_t
eecs427:l03_p13_t.caption: Folding a wide transistor into two fingers shares the drain between them and reduces diffusion capacitance.
eecs427:l03_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p02_b.name: l04_p02_b
eecs427:l04_p02_b.caption: Gate delay in units of tau splits into effort delay f = gh and parasitic delay p.
eecs427:l04_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p03_t.name: l04_p03_t
eecs427:l04_p03_t.caption: On a delay-versus-fanout plot, g is the slope and p is the intercept, with the inverter as the reference g = p = 1.
eecs427:l04_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p03_b.name: l04_p03_b
eecs427:l04_p03_b.caption: Logical effort is the input capacitance of a gate divided by that of an inverter delivering the same output current, so inverter 3/3, NAND2 4/3, NOR2 5/3.
eecs427:l04_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p04_t.name: l04_p04_t
eecs427:l04_p04_t.caption: For a 2:1 reference, an n-input NAND has g = (n+2)/3 and an n-input NOR has g = (2n+1)/3.
eecs427:l04_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p04_b.name: l04_p04_b
eecs427:l04_p04_b.caption: Parasitic delay is estimated from output self-loading at equal drive: inverter 3/3 = 1, NAND2 6/3 = 2, NOR2 6/3 = 2.
eecs427:l04_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p05_b.name: l04_p05_b
eecs427:l04_p05_b.caption: Normalized delay versus electrical effort shows lines whose slope is g and intercept is p, for example a NAND3 at d = (5/3)h + 3.
eecs427:l04_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p06_t.name: l04_p06_t
eecs427:l04_p06_t.caption: An inverter driving four copies of itself has h = 4, g = 1, p = 1, so the FO4 delay is 5 tau, roughly L/3 ps.
eecs427:l04_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p06_b.name: l04_p06_b
eecs427:l04_p06_b.caption: A gate with Cin = 1 driving three loads totaling 3 has h = 3, and as a NAND4 with g = 6/3 and p = 4 its delay is 10 tau.
eecs427:l04_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p07_b.name: l04_p07_b
eecs427:l04_p07_b.caption: With branching, part of the current goes off-path, so the product of stage efforts exceeds H and must include the branching effort b.
eecs427:l04_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p08_t.name: l04_p08_t
eecs427:l04_p08_t.caption: Path effort F = GBH is the product of stage efforts and depends only on topology, not on sizes or added inverters.
eecs427:l04_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p08_b.name: l04_p08_b
eecs427:l04_p08_b.caption: Setting the derivative of total delay with respect to h1 to zero gives g1h1 = g2h2, so delay is minimal when stage efforts are equal.
eecs427:l04_p08_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p09_t.name: l04_p09_t
eecs427:l04_p09_t.caption: For N stages the optimum stage effort is F to the 1/N, and the minimum path delay is N times F to the 1/N plus P.
eecs427:l04_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p09_b.name: l04_p09_b
eecs427:l04_p09_b.caption: Three NAND2 stages from Cin = 4 to CL = 108 have F = 64, an optimal stage effort of 4 and a minimum delay of 18 tau.
eecs427:l04_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p10_b.name: l04_p10_b
eecs427:l04_p10_b.caption: Working backward from the load with Cin = g·Cout/f gives input caps 36, 12 and 4, and the last NAND2 uses transistors of width 18.
eecs427:l04_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p11_t.name: l04_p11_t
eecs427:l04_p11_t.caption: Adding n2 inverters leaves F unchanged but adds parasitic delay, so the optimum number of stages is a balance that depends on technology.
eecs427:l04_p11_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p11_b.name: l04_p11_b
eecs427:l04_p11_b.caption: With p_inv = 1 the best number of stages rises by one roughly every factor of 4 in path effort, and the best stage effort stays between about 2.4 and 4.4.
eecs427:l04_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p13_t.name: l04_p13_t
eecs427:l04_p13_t.caption: A 4-to-16 decoder for a 16-word by 32-bit register file drives 96 units of wordline capacitance from address inputs of 10 units each.
eecs427:l04_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p13_b.name: l04_p13_b
eecs427:l04_p13_b.caption: With H = 9.6, B = 8, G = 2, F = 153.6 the best design is 3 stages with stage effort 5.35, delay 22.1 tau, and sizes 10, 6.7 and 18.
eecs427:l04_p13_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p14_t.name: l04_p14_t
eecs427:l04_p14_t.caption: A spreadsheet comparison of decoder topologies shows NAND2-INV-NAND2-INV is fastest at 19.7 tau and a single NOR4 is terrible at 234 tau.
eecs427:l04_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p14_b.name: l04_p14_b
eecs427:l04_p14_b.caption: Using more stages than optimal is less harmful than using fewer: delay is 1.51 times optimal at half the stages but only 1.26 times at double.
eecs427:l04_p14_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p15_t.name: l04_p15_t
eecs427:l04_p15_t.caption: Sizing a single gate wrong by 1.5x or 0.67x costs only about 4 percent of delay, and even 2x or 0.5x costs about 13 percent.
eecs427:l04_p15_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p15_b.name: l04_p15_b
eecs427:l04_p15_b.caption: P/N = 2 balances noise margins and slopes, but P/N = 1.5 lowers input capacitance and can give a faster average delay.
eecs427:l04_p15_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p16_t.name: l04_p16_t
eecs427:l04_p16_t.caption: Internal-node capacitance and body effect make the bottom and middle inputs of a stack slower, which the simple logical-effort model ignores.
eecs427:l04_p16_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l04_p19_t.name: l04_p19_t
eecs427:l04_p19_t.caption: Measured in the class's 130 nm process, tau is about 6.3 ps and p_inv about 3.4 at nominal, with clear spread across fast and slow corners.
eecs427:l04_p19_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p01_b.name: l05_p01_b
eecs427:l05_p01_b.caption: A full adder is S = A⊕B⊕C and Cout = MAJ(A,B,C); the truth table splits into kill, propagate and generate rows.
eecs427:l05_p01_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p02_t.name: l05_p02_t
eecs427:l05_p02_t.caption: Generate, propagate and kill describe what a bit does to the incoming carry, using only A and B.
eecs427:l05_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p02_b.name: l05_p02_b
eecs427:l05_p02_b.caption: Carry and sum can be written as Co = G + P·Ci and S = P⊕Ci, and P = A+B works for the carry but not the sum.
eecs427:l05_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p03_t.name: l05_p03_t
eecs427:l05_p03_t.caption: The 28-transistor static adder computes ¬Cout first and then reuses it to build the sum.
eecs427:l05_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p03_b.name: l05_p03_b
eecs427:l05_p03_b.caption: Inverting all inputs inverts both outputs, so a ripple chain can alternate true and complemented bits and drop inverters.
eecs427:l05_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p04_t.name: l05_p04_t
eecs427:l05_p04_t.caption: The 24-transistor mirror adder uses symmetric NMOS and PMOS networks, with Ci transistors placed closest to the output.
eecs427:l05_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p04_b.name: l05_p04_b
eecs427:l05_p04_b.caption: Layout rules for the mirror adder focus on minimizing capacitance at the carry node Co.
eecs427:l05_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p05_t.name: l05_p05_t
eecs427:l05_p05_t.caption: Ripple carry delay grows linearly with the number of bits, so the goal is the fastest possible carry cell.
eecs427:l05_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p05_b.name: l05_p05_b
eecs427:l05_p05_b.caption: Using P and G, the ripple adder splits into a setup stage, a carry chain of AND-OR cells, and a sum XOR.
eecs427:l05_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p06_t.name: l05_p06_t
eecs427:l05_p06_t.caption: Carry-bypass skips a block when all its bits propagate, selecting Cin directly via a mux.
eecs427:l05_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p06_b.name: l05_p06_b
eecs427:l05_p06_b.caption: The bypass critical path ripples through the first block, bypasses the middle blocks, and ripples through the last block.
eecs427:l05_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p07_b.name: l05_p07_b
eecs427:l05_p07_b.caption: The carry-select adder precomputes both possible block carries and a multiplexer picks the right one when the real carry arrives.
eecs427:l05_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p08_t.name: l05_p08_t
eecs427:l05_p08_t.caption: In a linear carry-select adder the critical path is one block ripple plus one mux per block.
eecs427:l05_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p09_t.name: l05_p09_t
eecs427:l05_p09_t.caption: Square-root carry select grows block sizes by one so each block's carries are ready just as the incoming carry arrives.
eecs427:l05_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p09_b.name: l05_p09_b
eecs427:l05_p09_b.caption: Ripple is linear, linear-select grows in steps, and square-root select grows slowest with word length.
eecs427:l05_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p10_b.name: l05_p10_b
eecs427:l05_p10_b.caption: Black cells combine group generate and propagate, gray cells compute only generate, and buffers just pass signals.
eecs427:l05_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p11_t.name: l05_p11_t
eecs427:l05_p11_t.caption: The ripple adder drawn as a PG diagram is a serial chain of N−1 gray cells.
eecs427:l05_p11_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p11_b.name: l05_p11_b
eecs427:l05_p11_b.caption: Kogge-Stone reaches every group G in log2N levels with fanout of 2, at the cost of many long wires.
eecs427:l05_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p12_t.name: l05_p12_t
eecs427:l05_p12_t.caption: Brent-Kung uses a forward tree and a backward tree, giving low fanout and few wires but 2log2(n)−1 levels.
eecs427:l05_p12_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p12_b.name: l05_p12_b
eecs427:l05_p12_b.caption: Sklansky reaches log2(n) levels with few wires but fanout that doubles each level and uneven sizing.
eecs427:l05_p12_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p13_t.name: l05_p13_t
eecs427:l05_p13_t.caption: Every prefix tree trades logic levels, fanout and wiring, and the three corners are Kogge-Stone, Brent-Kung and Sklansky.
eecs427:l05_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p13_b.name: l05_p13_b
eecs427:l05_p13_b.caption: Han-Carlson does Kogge-Stone on every other bit and one ripple stage at the end, halving wiring.
eecs427:l05_p13_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p14_t.name: l05_p14_t
eecs427:l05_p14_t.caption: Knowles halves Kogge-Stone wiring by letting neighbors share overlapping groups, at the cost of more fanout.
eecs427:l05_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p14_b.name: l05_p14_b
eecs427:l05_p14_b.caption: Ladner-Fischer mixes Brent-Kung, Sklansky and Han-Carlson layers to trade logic levels against fanout with low wiring.
eecs427:l05_p14_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p15_t.name: l05_p15_t
eecs427:l05_p15_t.caption: A higher-radix cell merges four groups at once, G = G3 + P3(G2 + P2(G1 + P1G0)).
eecs427:l05_p15_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l05_p16_t.name: l05_p16_t
eecs427:l05_p16_t.caption: Sparse trees compute only every s-th carry and use carry-select blocks to finish the sums.
eecs427:l05_p16_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p02_t.name: l06_p02_t
eecs427:l06_p02_t.caption: Static CMOS is ratioless, full-swing and nearly zero static power, which is why it is the default.
eecs427:l06_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p03_t.name: l06_p03_t
eecs427:l06_p03_t.caption: A pulse-static path is reset to a known state by a clock and then evaluates with only one transition per gate.
eecs427:l06_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p04_b.name: l06_p04_b
eecs427:l06_p04_b.caption: Because each gate in evaluation only switches one way, its P/N ratio can be skewed to speed that edge.
eecs427:l06_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p05_t.name: l06_p05_t
eecs427:l06_p05_t.caption: PS-CMOS is fast through skewing, has no delay dependence on history, and does not glitch in evaluation.
eecs427:l06_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p05_b.name: l06_p05_b
eecs427:l06_p05_b.caption: PS-CMOS cannot make arbitrary connections, burns more power, and has worse noise margin from skewed ratios.
eecs427:l06_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p06_t.name: l06_p06_t
eecs427:l06_p06_t.caption: DCVS uses complementary NMOS pull-down trees with a cross-coupled PMOS pair as the load.
eecs427:l06_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p08_t.name: l06_p08_t
eecs427:l06_p08_t.caption: In DCVS the side pulled down by the NMOS tree moves first, then the cross-coupled PMOS pulls the other side up.
eecs427:l06_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p09_t.name: l06_p09_t
eecs427:l06_p09_t.caption: DCVS needs no PMOS duality, so input capacitance is lower and complex functions fit in one stage.
eecs427:l06_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p09_b.name: l06_p09_b
eecs427:l06_p09_b.caption: DCVS needs dual-rail inputs, has crowbar current, and the PMOS must be sized in a narrow window.
eecs427:l06_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p10_t.name: l06_p10_t
eecs427:l06_p10_t.caption: CNTL adds clamp transistors so internal nodes swing only between about Vt and Vdd−Vt.
eecs427:l06_p10_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p13_t.name: l06_p13_t
eecs427:l06_p13_t.caption: CNTL rises faster and draws a smaller current spike because the PMOS is never hard on or off.
eecs427:l06_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p13_b.name: l06_p13_b
eecs427:l06_p13_b.caption: CNTL pays with higher leakage, more devices, careful sizing, and a non-full-swing output that must be restored.
eecs427:l06_p13_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p14_t.name: l06_p14_t
eecs427:l06_p14_t.caption: Pass-gate logic is 20–50% faster in XOR- and mux-like circuits because it carries less capacitance.
eecs427:l06_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p14_b.name: l06_p14_b
eecs427:l06_p14_b.caption: Pass gates lose a threshold, suffer body effect, and are vulnerable to input undershoot and coupling.
eecs427:l06_p14_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p15_t.name: l06_p15_t
eecs427:l06_p15_t.caption: Pass-gate delay depends on state, and the output needs an inverter before it can drive the next stage.
eecs427:l06_p15_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p15_b.name: l06_p15_b
eecs427:l06_p15_b.caption: LEAP adds an output inverter with a PMOS feedback keeper to restore full swing.
eecs427:l06_p15_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p16_t.name: l06_p16_t
eecs427:l06_p16_t.caption: With a keeper the internal node reaches full rail, but the input sees more loading and current during switching.
eecs427:l06_p16_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p18_t.name: l06_p18_t
eecs427:l06_p18_t.caption: Transmission gates pair NMOS and PMOS so either level passes cleanly, with better noise margin but more capacitance.
eecs427:l06_p18_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p18_b.name: l06_p18_b
eecs427:l06_p18_b.caption: Simulated side by side, the transmission gate reaches the full rail while the NMOS pass gate stops short.
eecs427:l06_p18_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p19_t.name: l06_p19_t
eecs427:l06_p19_t.caption: CPL builds dual-rail NMOS pass networks with a cross-coupled PMOS restorer and output inverters.
eecs427:l06_p19_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p20_b.name: l06_p20_b
eecs427:l06_p20_b.caption: Unlike DCVS, CPL inputs drive both trees and PMOS sizing affects only speed and noise margin.
eecs427:l06_p20_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p21_t.name: l06_p21_t
eecs427:l06_p21_t.caption: CPL is fast but has poor noise margin, needs buffered inputs, and its PMOS size trades noise and power against speed.
eecs427:l06_p21_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p22_b.name: l06_p22_b
eecs427:l06_p22_b.caption: OPL predicts every output is 1, so in an inverting path half the gates never need to switch.
eecs427:l06_p22_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p24_t.name: l06_p24_t
eecs427:l06_p24_t.caption: Precharging toward the middle and evaluating early cuts delay versus a classic dynamic gate.
eecs427:l06_p24_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p24_b.name: l06_p24_b
eecs427:l06_p24_b.caption: Clock timing relative to inputs decides whether the OPL output glitches down and recovers or stays high.
eecs427:l06_p24_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l06_p25_b.name: l06_p25_b
eecs427:l06_p25_b.caption: OPL gates swing about half rail and are over 2x faster than CMOS, but clocking, variation and power make them hard to use.
eecs427:l06_p25_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p02_t.name: l07_p02_t
eecs427:l07_p02_t.caption: A dynamic gate precharges its node high when the clock is low and conditionally discharges it through the NMOS network when the clock is high.
eecs427:l07_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p02_b.name: l07_p02_b
eecs427:l07_p02_b.caption: The dynamic 3-input OR has far less input and internal capacitance than the static version.
eecs427:l07_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p03_t.name: l07_p03_t
eecs427:l07_p03_t.caption: Domino is faster with lower input capacitance and an early switch point, using a HI-skew output inverter.
eecs427:l07_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p03_b.name: l07_p03_b
eecs427:l07_p03_b.caption: Domino pays with low noise margin, charge sharing, leakage, and a noise-sensitive floating node.
eecs427:l07_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p04_t.name: l07_p04_t
eecs427:l07_p04_t.caption: During evaluate a non-discharged dynamic node floats, and NMOS leakage slowly discharges it.
eecs427:l07_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p04_b.name: l07_p04_b
eecs427:l07_p04_b.caption: The keeper current must sit between the total off-leakage of the pull-down and the on-current of a single pull-down path.
eecs427:l07_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p05_t.name: l07_p05_t
eecs427:l07_p05_t.caption: A static PMOS pull-up network as keeper avoids the fight, but only a few PMOS fit in series and input cap rises.
eecs427:l07_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p05_b.name: l07_p05_b
eecs427:l07_p05_b.caption: In evaluate the dynamic node shares charge with an internal node that was discharged in a previous cycle.
eecs427:l07_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p06_t.name: l07_p06_t
eecs427:l07_p06_t.caption: Precharging internal nodes fixes charge sharing but adds capacitance and makes the pull-down slower.
eecs427:l07_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p06_b.name: l07_p06_b
eecs427:l07_p06_b.caption: Domino delay depends on input arrival time, and the first gate in a chain sees extra clock-related delay.
eecs427:l07_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p07_t.name: l07_p07_t
eecs427:l07_p07_t.caption: A domino chain precharges every gate together and then evaluates in a ripple, with inputs held stable by latches during evaluate.
eecs427:l07_p07_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p07_b.name: l07_p07_b
eecs427:l07_p07_b.caption: Only the first stage needs a footer, provided later stages see their inputs precharge low before their own precharge.
eecs427:l07_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p08_t.name: l07_p08_t
eecs427:l07_p08_t.caption: Delayed clocks let each stage precharge after its inputs have fallen and evaluate before its inputs become valid.
eecs427:l07_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p09_t.name: l07_p09_t
eecs427:l07_p09_t.caption: Footless domino needs multiple clocks and gives later stages less precharge time, traded against one less series NMOS.
eecs427:l07_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p09_b.name: l07_p09_b
eecs427:l07_p09_b.caption: NORA alternates N-type gates precharged high with P-type gates precharged low, with no inverter in between.
eecs427:l07_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p10_b.name: l07_p10_b
eecs427:l07_p10_b.caption: NORA is fast but drives loads poorly, uses slow PMOS networks, and has poor noise margin.
eecs427:l07_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p11_t.name: l07_p11_t
eecs427:l07_p11_t.caption: Dual-rail domino computes both f and its complement so any logic function is possible, at twice the transistors.
eecs427:l07_p11_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p11_b.name: l07_p11_b
eecs427:l07_p11_b.caption: When evaluation trees share internal nodes, those nodes are precharged for every input pattern.
eecs427:l07_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p12_t.name: l07_p12_t
eecs427:l07_p12_t.caption: Cross-coupled keepers in dual-rail domino avoid a keeper fight but leave both rails unprotected until inputs arrive.
eecs427:l07_p12_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p12_b.name: l07_p12_b
eecs427:l07_p12_b.caption: Multiple-output domino taps intermediate nodes of one pull-down stack to compute several functions at once.
eecs427:l07_p12_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p13_t.name: l07_p13_t
eecs427:l07_p13_t.caption: Compound domino ends short dynamic stacks in a static gate, e.g. a NAND that computes AB + CD.
eecs427:l07_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p14_t.name: l07_p14_t
eecs427:l07_p14_t.caption: Self-resetting domino has no clock or footer; its own output, delayed through an inverter chain, triggers the precharge.
eecs427:l07_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p17_b.name: l07_p17_b
eecs427:l07_p17_b.caption: SRD requires inputs to fall before the reset pulse and the reset to finish before the next input arrives.
eecs427:l07_p17_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p18_b.name: l07_p18_b
eecs427:l07_p18_b.caption: SRD trades the clock for hard pulse-timing constraints that are sensitive to process variation.
eecs427:l07_p18_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p19_t.name: l07_p19_t
eecs427:l07_p19_t.caption: LSDL puts a clocked latch behind a dynamic front end so the output changes only when its value changes.
eecs427:l07_p19_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p20_t.name: l07_p20_t
eecs427:l07_p20_t.caption: In LSDL the dynamic node precharges every cycle, but the latched output switches only on a real change.
eecs427:l07_p20_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p21_t.name: l07_p21_t
eecs427:l07_p21_t.caption: LSDL gives up keepers and dynamic depth per stage, needs narrow evaluate pulses, and complicates setup and hold analysis.
eecs427:l07_p21_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p22_t.name: l07_p22_t
eecs427:l07_p22_t.caption: When a static gate driven by a dynamic node turns on, its rising gate capacitance pulls charge off the dynamic node.
eecs427:l07_p22_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l07_p22_b.name: l07_p22_b
eecs427:l07_p22_b.caption: Clock feedthrough through the precharge device's gate-drain capacitance bumps the dynamic node at clock edges.
eecs427:l07_p22_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p02_t.name: l08_p02_t
eecs427:l08_p02_t.caption: Total power splits into dynamic switching, short-circuit (crowbar) and static leakage components.
eecs427:l08_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p02_b.name: l08_p02_b
eecs427:l08_p02_b.caption: Short-circuit current is a brief overlap blip, under 10% of dynamic power when input and output slopes are comparable.
eecs427:l08_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p03_t.name: l08_p03_t
eecs427:l08_p03_t.caption: On a rising output the supply delivers C·VDD², half burned in the pMOS and half stored on the load.
eecs427:l08_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p03_b.name: l08_p03_b
eecs427:l08_p03_b.caption: On the falling output the supply delivers nothing and the stored ½C·VDD² is dissipated in the nMOS.
eecs427:l08_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p04_t.name: l08_p04_t
eecs427:l08_p04_t.caption: Dynamic power is α·C·VDD²·f, with α = 1 for a clock and ½ for a node that toggles once per cycle.
eecs427:l08_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p04_b.name: l08_p04_b
eecs427:l08_p04_b.caption: For random independent data α = P·(1−P), giving 0.25 at P = 0.5 and typically about 0.1 in real logic.
eecs427:l08_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p05_t.name: l08_p05_t
eecs427:l08_p05_t.caption: Output-high probability for each gate follows from the input probabilities, assuming independent inputs.
eecs427:l08_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p05_b.name: l08_p05_b
eecs427:l08_p05_b.caption: A 4-input AND built as NAND2-NAND2 into an inverted-input AND (a NOR2) has α = 3/16 on the internal nodes and 15/256 on the output.
eecs427:l08_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p06_t.name: l08_p06_t
eecs427:l08_p06_t.caption: A 1-billion-transistor 65 nm chip at 1 V and 1 GHz, with logic at α = 0.1 and memory at α = 0.02.
eecs427:l08_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p06_b.name: l08_p06_b
eecs427:l08_p06_b.caption: Switched capacitance is 27 nF of logic and 171 nF of memory, giving about 6.1 W of dynamic power.
eecs427:l08_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p07_t.name: l08_p07_t
eecs427:l08_p07_t.caption: Under ideal (Dennard) scaling, power per device falls as 1/S² and power density stays constant.
eecs427:l08_p07_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p07_b.name: l08_p07_b
eecs427:l08_p07_b.caption: Power rose anyway because device count grew, VDD stopped scaling, leakage grew and interconnect increased.
eecs427:l08_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p10_t.name: l08_p10_t
eecs427:l08_p10_t.caption: A transmission-gate latch with a local clock inverter puts 8C on clock, while a pass-nMOS latch moves the load to data (14C data, 2C clock).
eecs427:l08_p10_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p10_b.name: l08_p10_b
eecs427:l08_p10_b.caption: Clock gating stops the clock to idle registers, removing α = 1 clock switching and all downstream activity.
eecs427:l08_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p11_b.name: l08_p11_b
eecs427:l08_p11_b.caption: The reference datapath (adder + comparator) runs at 40 MHz at 5 V with switched capacitance Cref.
eecs427:l08_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p12_t.name: l08_p12_t
eecs427:l08_p12_t.caption: Two parallel copies at half clock rate allow VDD = Vref/1.7, giving 0.36 Pref at 2.15× capacitance.
eecs427:l08_p12_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p12_b.name: l08_p12_b
eecs427:l08_p12_b.caption: Pipelining halves the critical path so VDD = Vref/1.7 at the same clock, giving 0.39 Pref with only 1.15× capacitance.
eecs427:l08_p12_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p13_t.name: l08_p13_t
eecs427:l08_p13_t.caption: Summary: pipelined 0.39, parallel 0.36, pipeline plus parallel 0.2 of reference power at 2.0 V and 3.7× area.
eecs427:l08_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p14_t.name: l08_p14_t
eecs427:l08_p14_t.caption: Two supplies are common; a low-VDD gate driving a high-VDD gate needs a level converter because the pMOS never fully turns off.
eecs427:l08_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p14_b.name: l08_p14_b
eecs427:l08_p14_b.caption: The DCVS level converter uses cross-coupled pMOS and differential nMOS pull-downs, at the cost of contention and more transistors.
eecs427:l08_p14_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p15_t.name: l08_p15_t
eecs427:l08_p15_t.caption: The pass-gate level converter lets a VDDL-gated pass nMOS pull the input node low, with a single pMOS feedback keeper, reducing contention.
eecs427:l08_p15_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p15_b.name: l08_p15_b
eecs427:l08_p15_b.caption: A diode-connected Vt-drop transistor avoids a second supply, giving swing Vt to VDD−Vt and power α·C·VDD·(VDD−2Vt)·f.
eecs427:l08_p15_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p16_b.name: l08_p16_b
eecs427:l08_p16_b.caption: Intel's dual-supply latch accepts a low-VDD clock on nMOS-only clock devices; the test chip cut clock power by 71%.
eecs427:l08_p16_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l08_p17_t.name: l08_p17_t
eecs427:l08_p17_t.caption: Clock/power gating saves energy linearly with duty cycle, while just-in-time DVFS saves roughly with the cube.
eecs427:l08_p17_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p02_t.name: l09_p02_t
eecs427:l09_p02_t.caption: I1 is reverse-biased junction leakage, typically below 1 fA/µm² and negligible, plus band-to-band tunneling.
eecs427:l09_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p02_b.name: l09_p02_b
eecs427:l09_p02_b.caption: I2 is subthreshold (weak-inversion) conduction, the dominant leakage in modern devices.
eecs427:l09_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p03_t.name: l09_p03_t
eecs427:l09_p03_t.caption: Subthreshold current is exponential in Vgs; rewriting it relative to Ioff gives a base-10 form with slope S ≈ 100 mV/decade.
eecs427:l09_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p03_b.name: l09_p03_b
eecs427:l09_p03_b.caption: DIBL lowers the threshold by η·Vds, so higher drain voltage increases leakage.
eecs427:l09_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p04_t.name: l09_p04_t
eecs427:l09_p04_t.caption: Reverse body bias raises Vt and cuts leakage; leakage is flat in Vds above 4vT (except DIBL) and drops sharply below 2vT.
eecs427:l09_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p04_b.name: l09_p04_b
eecs427:l09_p04_b.caption: I3 is gate-induced drain leakage: with negative gate and positive drain, tunneling at the drain edge under the gate.
eecs427:l09_p04_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p05_t.name: l09_p05_t
eecs427:l09_p05_t.caption: On log Ids vs Vgs: S = 100 mV/decade, DIBL moves Ioff from 2.0 to 27 nA/µm between Vds = 0.1 and 1.0 V, and GIDL lifts the curve at negative Vgs.
eecs427:l09_p05_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p05_b.name: l09_p05_b
eecs427:l09_p05_b.caption: For Vds above 50 mV, Isub ≈ Ioff·10^((Vgs + η(Vds−VDD) − kγVsb)/S), with typical 65 nm values Ioff = 1–100 nA/µm and η = kγ = 0.1.
eecs427:l09_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p06_t.name: l09_p06_t
eecs427:l09_p06_t.caption: I4 is gate-oxide tunneling, rising sharply with thinner oxide and depending strongly on oxide material.
eecs427:l09_p06_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p06_b.name: l09_p06_b
eecs427:l09_p06_b.caption: Gate leakage is exponentially sensitive to tox and VDD, larger for electrons (nMOS), negligible above 30 Å and critical near 12 Å until high-k.
eecs427:l09_p06_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p07_t.name: l09_p07_t
eecs427:l09_p07_t.caption: The three levers: +100 mV of Vt cuts leakage ~10× but slows the gate, cooling cuts it ~5.2× per 10 °C, and stacking cuts it further.
eecs427:l09_p07_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p07_b.name: l09_p07_b
eecs427:l09_p07_b.caption: Two series OFF devices self-reverse-bias: Vx = ηVDD/(1 + 2η + kγ) and leakage drops about 10×.
eecs427:l09_p07_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p08_t.name: l09_p08_t
eecs427:l09_p08_t.caption: Simulated stack leakage: SVT 258 → 36.1 → 19.8 pA for 1/2/3-stacks; HVT 1.25 → 0.185 → 0.122 pA.
eecs427:l09_p08_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p08_b.name: l09_p08_b
eecs427:l09_p08_b.caption: In a NAND3, leakage ranges from 10.5 pA (all inputs 0) to 192 pA (all 1); dominant states have only one OFF device in the path.
eecs427:l09_p08_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p09_t.name: l09_p09_t
eecs427:l09_p09_t.caption: Single-gate leakage varies up to 101× across states, but whole blocks vary only 1.2–1.8× because many gates average out.
eecs427:l09_p09_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p09_b.name: l09_p09_b
eecs427:l09_p09_b.caption: Find the minimum-leakage input vector (30–40% variation) and force it with sleep-controlled latches.
eecs427:l09_p09_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p10_t.name: l09_p10_t
eecs427:l09_p10_t.caption: Power gating uses high-Vt header/footer switches to create virtual rails, with output isolation; the switch costs IR drop when on and dynamic power to toggle.
eecs427:l09_p10_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p10_b.name: l09_p10_b
eecs427:l09_p10_b.caption: A state-retaining MTCMOS latch keeps a high-Vt, always-powered storage loop so data survives standby.
eecs427:l09_p10_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p11_b.name: l09_p11_b
eecs427:l09_p11_b.caption: Use low Vt only on critical paths; assignment per gate or per transistor needs no clustering and no level converters.
eecs427:l09_p11_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p12_t.name: l09_p12_t
eecs427:l09_p12_t.caption: Vt can be assigned per gate, per pull-up/pull-down half, per stack, or per transistor, with finer control costing library size and design-rule area.
eecs427:l09_p12_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p12_b.name: l09_p12_b
eecs427:l09_p12_b.caption: Dynamic body bias applies about 450 mV forward bias in active mode for speed and about 500 mV reverse bias in idle mode for leakage, needing a triple well.
eecs427:l09_p12_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p13_t.name: l09_p13_t
eecs427:l09_p13_t.caption: VTCMOS biases the n-well and an isolated p-well separately (VBBP, VBBN) to move Vt at run time.
eecs427:l09_p13_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p13_b.name: l09_p13_b
eecs427:l09_p13_b.caption: Four techniques: MTCMOS (high-Vt switches), dual-Vt, state assignment, and variable-Vt via substrate bias.
eecs427:l09_p13_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l09_p14_t.name: l09_p14_t
eecs427:l09_p14_t.caption: Dynamic and leakage power knobs sorted by design time, run time, and adaptive (variable throughput).
eecs427:l09_p14_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p01_b.name: l10_p01_b
eecs427:l10_p01_b.caption: An SRAM is a 2^n-row by 2^m-column array of cells with a row decoder, bitline conditioning on top and column circuitry at the bottom.
eecs427:l10_p01_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p02_t.name: l10_p02_t
eecs427:l10_p02_t.caption: The 6T cell stores a bit in cross-coupled inverters and reaches the bitlines through two access transistors gated by the wordline.
eecs427:l10_p02_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p02_b.name: l10_p02_b
eecs427:l10_p02_b.caption: The SNM is the side of the largest square that fits inside the butterfly curve's lobes, here 0.32 V.
eecs427:l10_p02_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p03_t.name: l10_p03_t
eecs427:l10_p03_t.caption: During a read the bitline on the 0 side discharges through access and pull-down devices, and the 0 node bumps up.
eecs427:l10_p03_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p03_b.name: l10_p03_b
eecs427:l10_p03_b.caption: The access transistor and pull-down NMOS form a divider that raises node A while bit discharges.
eecs427:l10_p03_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p04_t.name: l10_p04_t
eecs427:l10_p04_t.caption: The read bump on node A falls as the cell ratio rises, so a CR around 1.2 to 2 keeps the bump well below the trip point.
eecs427:l10_p04_t.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p05_b.name: l10_p05_b
eecs427:l10_p05_b.caption: Sizing order: pull-down strong, access medium, pull-up weak.
eecs427:l10_p05_b.provenance: Existing original slide image; exact source-caption match and within-page order verified

eecs427:l10_p04_b.name: l10_p04_b
